rules.title: Berkeley ban on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement:
It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley (§ 13.63.030(A)). It is also unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels (§ 13.63.030(B)).

Definitions (§ 13.63.020):
- A coordinated pricing algorithm is any analytical or computational process that uses Competitor Data to recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates or other rental contract terms for future leases in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor.
- Competitor Data is non-public data on actual rents, occupancy and lease dates for properties the landlord does not own or manage, when the data is less than 90 days old.

Violations: each month a violation continues, and each unit for which the algorithm was used, is a separate violation.

Remedies (§ 13.63.040):
- The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
- An aggrieved tenant may sue over landlord use for injunctive relief, money damages and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
- The prevailing City Attorney or tenant is awarded reasonable attorney's fees and costs. A lease clause limiting tenant fees is unenforceable.

The chapter does not regulate rent amounts and does not bar software that helps landlords manage units generally or through public data.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation; Competitor Data = non-public data less than 90 days old; mandatory attorney's fees to the prevailing City Attorney or tenant

coverage.summary: All residential dwelling units in Berkeley. Applies to landlords who use coordinated pricing algorithms and to vendors who sell, license or provide them to Berkeley landlords. No unit-count, building-age or landlord-size limits.
coverage.other_conditions: Excluded products: (a) aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that make no recommendations; (b) tools for setting rent or income limits under affordable-housing guidelines; (c) market research for project financing, appraisals, and research, testing or training for software development, provided Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated. Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act common pricing algorithm rule (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729).

rules.exemptions: Aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that make no recommendations; products setting rent or income limits under government affordable-housing guidelines; market research for project financing, appraisals, and software research, testing or training (Competitor Data not used as a live input).
rules.effective_date_note: The captured ordinance text states no effective date or final adoption date. It records only that the ordinance was passed to print and ordered published at the Council meeting of Nov. 18, 2025 (8 ayes, 0 noes, 1 absent). The secondary Morgan Lewis alert (DX06, Aug. 21, 2026) gives 'effective January 2026' (month only). Status is in_force because any candidate effective date precedes the query date.

It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies (BMC ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement:
Disclosure (BMC 13.78.010): an owner or agent who charges a fee to buy a consumer credit report and to process an application must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). The disclosure may be in the rental application or in a separate disclosure, and must be given before the fee is received.

Existing tenants (BMC 13.78.016): an owner or agent may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees for a roommate's departure or for a request to add or replace a roommate.

Applicability (BMC 13.78.018): chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language, and conflicting lease provisions are unenforceable.
rules.key_value: Fee-rights statement and state fee-cap disclosure required before collecting a screening fee; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants. The dollar cap is set by state law (the Rent Board lists $68.96 for 2026).

coverage.other_conditions: Complementary to Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6, which sets the fee cap, receipt, credit-report and refund rules.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance Annual General Adjustment (AGA) limit on rent increases, 5% cap (Measure BB) and 2026 AGA of 1.0%
rules.requirement:
Landlords of fully covered units may raise rent each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) set by the Rent Board. The AGA is 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase, a formula approved by voters in November 2004 (BMC 13.76.110A).

Measure BB (November 2024) caps the AGA at 5%. A landlord with banked (unused) prior AGAs may still exceed 5% to reach the rent ceiling.

2026 AGA (Rent Board Regulation 1148, adopted Oct. 16, 2025):
- 1.0% on 2025 permanent rent ceilings, no earlier than Jan. 1, 2026.
- It may not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after Jan. 1, 2025 whose rents were set under Costa-Hawkins.
- Regulation 1148 sets the conditions for qualifying and the required tenant notice.

Other Measure BB rules:
- Government-owned or -subsidized units registered as fully covered get rent ceilings.
- For tenancies from Feb. 6, 2024, utility charges in fully covered units must be part of base rent unless separately metered in the tenant's name.
- Owners may petition for rent increases only for completed capital improvements, not planned ones.
rules.key_value: AGA = 65% of Bay Area CPI-U, capped at 5% (banked AGAs may exceed 5% up to the rent ceiling); 2026 AGA 1.0% (65% of 1.5% CPI), no earlier than Jan. 1, 2026

These are most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, single-family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996, and rooming houses (single-family homes with five or more rooms rented individually). Partially covered units have no rent control. They include new construction with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980, single-family tenancies from Jan. 1, 1996, most condominiums and certain subsidized units. Exempt units are outside the ordinance.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance just cause for eviction, notice requirements and owner move-in relocation (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.requirement:
Tenants in fully or partially covered units may not be evicted without just cause (formerly 'good cause').

Measure BB changes to grounds:
- Nonpayment eviction is barred unless rental debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit (Oakland-Fremont HUD Metro FMR).
- A tenant cannot be evicted for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
- Lease-breach evictions require all of the following:
  - a mutually agreed material term;
  - substantial actual damage to the landlord;
  - unreasonable tenant behavior;
  - a prior notice to cease that specifies the term and describes the violation and harm.

Notices and filings:
- Every termination notice must state that advice is available from the Rent Board and give its housing counseling phone number and website.
- Copies of termination notices, notices to quit and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days of service.
- For tenancies starting on or after Dec. 20, 2024, landlords must give a Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days and post it in any interior common area.

Owner move-in relocation:
- Owners must pay relocation assistance in owner move-in evictions, indexed annually to inflation.
- From Jan. 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if debt is at least 1 month HUD FMR; termination documents filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days; tenant rights notice within 15 days (tenancies from Dec. 20, 2024); owner move-in relocation $19,413 standard + $6,471 for qualifying households from Jan. 1, 2026 (1.5% CPI adjustment)

rules.title: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance relocation assistance
rules.requirement: When an owner evicts tenants to remove a property from the rental housing market (Ellis Act withdrawal), the owner must pay the same relocation assistance as for an owner move-in eviction. The payments are indexed to inflation, and the Rent Board publishes the yearly increase. From Jan. 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471, a 1.5% CPI-U adjustment for San Francisco-Oakland-San Jose.
rules.key_value: Standard relocation payment $19,413; additional $6,471 for qualifying households; effective Jan. 1, 2026 (1.5% CPI-U adjustment)

coverage.other_conditions: The additional payment applies only to qualifying households, which are not defined in the documents.

rules.effective_date_note: Jan. 1, 2026 is the effective date of the 2026 adjusted amounts, approved by the Rent Board on Oct. 16, 2025. The underlying ordinance predates this, and its original effective date is not stated.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on the security deposit at the end of each year. If the tenant moves out before year end, the landlord must pay a prorated amount.
